Abstract:

This study focuses on the development and characterization of nano-oxide dispersed tungsten alloys, specifically for their application as kinetic energy penetrators. Tungsten, a material with a high melting point and density, is crucial for such high-performance applications, where properties like ductility, fracture toughness, and high strain rate resistance are paramount. This research addresses the inherent limitation of pure tungsten, its susceptibility to oxidation at elevated temperatures due to the formation of porous WO3.&nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp The study employed mechanical alloying as the primary fabrication technique, utilizing elemental powders of W, Ni, Mo, Nb, Zr, and nano-oxides like Y2O3, TiO2, and ZrO2. Mechanical alloying was conducted for 20 h in a planetary ball mill under controlled conditions with Ball to Powder weight ratio (BPR) 10:1 and 5:1. The consolidated powders were then subjected to comprehensive characterization.&nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbspX-ray Diffraction (XRD) analysis revealed the formation of W-Ni-Nb-Mo solid. Mechanically alloyed powders demonstrated significant crystallite size reduction (9.23 nm) of W, enhanced lattice strain, and the formation of solid solutions with elements like Ni, Nb, and Mo solid solutions and significant peak broadening of W, indicating crystallite size reduction with milling time. The effectiveness of Y2O3 and TiO2 in promoting Ni diffusion into the W lattice was observed.&nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp &nbsp A detailed investigation into the mechanical properties, including hardness, density, compressive strength, and wear was conducted, with a particular focus on the effect of zirconia addition. Sintering at 1150&degC with 10:1 BPR, shows maximum densification of 99.6% and hardness of 20.42 GPa due to activated sintering,&nbspmicrostructure refinement, and oxide dispersion strengthening in 78W-10Ni-5Nb-5Mo-1Zr-1(Y2O3) sample. Addition of 1% Zirconia was found to significantly enhance hardness due to its dispersion strengthening effect. While samples without zirconia achieved high relative densities. Microstructural analysis via SEM and TEM confirmed the grain refinement and uniform distribution of nanoparticles, which acted as grain boundary pinners. Elemental mapping supports the formation of W solid solution. The nano-oxides are contained both at the W matrix interface and inside the particles, according to both elemental mapping and HRTEM analysis. Zr acts as oxygen absorber and converts to ZrO2. Zr further promotes grain refinement, solid solution strengthening, and the dispersion strengthening effect. Alloy with Zr addition exhibits the highest compressive strength, of 2.55 GPa, along with a significant compressive strain of 9.69% at the point of maximum compressive load in 78W-10Ni-5Nb-5Mo-1Zr-1(Y2O3) [1150 &degC SPS and 10:1 BPR], which is due to improved ductility of W alloy making it useful for high strength application. Oxide additions enhance the wear resistance of W alloys by acting as&nbsphard reinforcements, minimum wear rate of 0.105 (mm3/N.m)&times10-5 in 79W-10Ni-5Nb-5Mo-1(Y2O3) sample [1200 &degC SPS and 10:1 BPR]. These hard reinforcement lead to the formation of a stable&nbspprotective oxide layer&nbspduring wear as explained in wear mechanism. Furthermore, the oxidation behaviour was critically examined, 79W-10Ni-5Nb-5Mo-1(Y2O3) alloy with 10:1 BPR sintered at 1200&degC significantly improved oxidation resistance by forming a protective barrier layer, leading to reduced weight loss. The high-temperature properties, including creep resistance and retained hardness, were also substantially enhanced by the presence of zirconia, making these alloys highly suitable for demanding applications in extreme thermal environments.
